proof_summary: Letting \(d=D(n)\), strip off its factors of \(2\) and \(5\) to obtain \(d'\mid d\), coprime to \(10\), with \(d\mid 10^P d'\); since \(n\equiv d\pmod 9\), the congruence \(9a\equiv10n\pmod{d'}\) has a solution \(0\le a<d'\le n\). Using \(a\) fixed-width decimal blocks of value \(1\) and \(n-a\) blocks of value \(10\), with width \(2\varphi(d')\), constructs a number \(V\) with digit sum \(n\) and \(d'\mid V\); multiplying by a sufficiently large power of \(10\) preserves that digit sum, makes the result exceed \(n\), and makes it divisible by \(d\).
